svg.text: The guest could not resolve the far tail. Bare metal can.
The earlier KVM sweep is kept so host-owned findings have a counter-example sitting beside them.
KVM guest
p99 noise on one arm: 1480 us.
Gap between all four arms: 293 us.
Noise on one arm was larger than the
gap between all four. The far tail could
not be read.
g++ 15.1.1. Same rustc.
No core controls. Hypervisor in the way.
Kept, not dropped. Same design, same code.
Bare metal (reported)
p99 noise on one arm: 0.8 us.
Gap between all four arms: 1.6 us.
Noise is smaller than the gap. Both p99
rows and both p99.9 rows clear Holm,
4 rows in all.
Far tail pooled, 3,360,051 to 3,360,084 calls.
Slowest Rust arm 50 us below fastest C++.
A second bare-metal host agrees.
What this licences
Speed and RSS results name the host. RQ2 and the seam structure do not.
Tail delay numbers from any single host are a thinner basis for a roll-out than they look.
That is why the earlier guest sweep is kept, not dropped. Chapter 6, ethical and professional reflection.
